thread:
samir: Heads-up — customer acme-corp reports all traffic routed to eu-west-1 even though they pinned us-east-1.

maria: any error codes? latency numbers?

samir: lots of 401s from us-east key, but requests getting served from eu-west. latency ~340ms to 620ms, egress up 3.7x in eu region.

ines: Account used dedicated capacity with sticky routing. Can you paste the failover config from the user?

samir: they used the console. Support pulled config:
```
{
  "failover_policy": {
    "sticky": true,
    "priority_indices": [1,0],
    "weights": ["60%","40%"]
  }
}
```

jason: Wait `priority_indices`? UI stores indexes 1-based. Backend expects 0-based. That will flip order.

maria: omg. that explains why eu ended up priority 0.

samir: repro steps for SRE:
1) create failover via console with two regions (us-east, eu-west)
2) reorder in UI so us-east first (UI writes [1,0])
3) backend interprets as [1,0] being positions -> treats index 1 as highest priority due to bug
4) requests go to eu-west

ines: Confirmed locally — UI's reorder component emits 1-based indexes when sticky=true. Patch in progress.

ops-bot: deploy job started for fix branch fix/priority-index-offset PR#1987

eng-oncall: Rolling a hotfix to staging, will propagate to prod in 10m. Workaround for affected customers: set explicit priority array via API.

maria: Workaround curl:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/acme/failover \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"failover_policy": {"sticky": true, "priority": ["us-east-1","eu-west-1"]}}'
```

samir: we applied workaround for acme-corp, traffic normalized. customer confirmed latency back to normal :thumbsup:

jason: filing postmortem, tagging billing to review egress spike; internal config audit to detect other UI->API index conversions.

maria: closing thread after prod patch. Thanks folks.
